method: tinygrad critical path = weighted longest path over /tmp/pipeline_serial_graph.jsonl lines 70-74 (596 nodes, 5 JIT groups). llama = one steady replay (762 kernels, 3902.7 us span) of CUPTI graph 6 in /tmp/llama_d512_20260817b.sqlite.
llama_fusion_fact: llama has NO separate elementwise add, reduce, scatter, or glu kernels. The logical DOT x*y / x+y / glu nodes are fused into mul_mat_vec_q epilogues or rms_norm_f32. This is the structural source of llama's short exposed-support time.

support_ledger_on_critical_path.note: reduce_output, residual, and scatter_vocab have no llama critical-path equivalent: llama fuses them into rms_norm_f32 and mul_mat_vec_q epilogues (or does the token scatter outside the CUDA graph).

proven_vs_inferred.proven: tinygrad carries 927.9 us of non-gemv support on its critical path; llama exposes only 310.6 us of non-mmq work. The delta of 617 us is concentrated in reduce_output (235), residual (135), scatter (56), and extra flash exposure (llama flash is 2 overlapped kernels with ~127 us exposed vs tinygrad's 314 us serialized).
proven_vs_inferred.inferred: Fusing tinygrad's reduce_output into the rms norm and the residual add into the gemv epilogue would remove ~370 us of separate kernels from every source-to-sink path. This is a structural guarantee (the chain gets no longer and loses those kernel boundaries), but the exact wall delta is a bounded measurement (launch/readback floor to ~426 us ceiling) and has not been A/B-tested yet.

next_action: Implement the two epilogue fusions (norm-reduce into rmsnorm; residual add into the O-gemv epilogue) plus the vocab-scatter fusion, then run the same-session flocked token-sha A/B against the 210.97 tok/s landed control.
